rows.en: He's a pretty nasty person
He's kind of scary
Yeah, he is.{p}

The warp in his heart was way worse than any ordinary student's.
A backlash, I guess you'd call it.
Apparently it's strongest in exactly the people who keep themselves held down.
Kawahara's heart was full of hatred for the guy.
If there really was a question sheet stuck in that textbook, why not sneak it into this guy's desk?
And then go rat him out to the teacher...{p}

"What's the matter?
You look pale."
That snapped Kawahara back to himself.
"No... it's nothing."
He left that classroom.{p}

During the next class, Kawahara thought it over.
That's it, he'd just tell the teacher the truth.
He was normally a good student, so surely they'd believe him.
...No, wait.
What if they thought his grades were good because he was always cheating somehow...
What if they thought he'd only come to return the question sheet because this time it happened to cause a fuss...
He kept thinking up all these needless things.{p}And this is the conclusion he came to.
Tell the truth after all
Throw out what's in the textbook

At the next break, Kawahara went up to the roof.
After making sure nobody was around, he went to open the textbook he'd hidden under his uniform.
It was really windy that day.
So whatever was inside the textbook wouldn't blow away, he moved over into a corner, out of the wind.
He was just nervously trying to peek inside, when...
The door to the roof slowly opened, and he saw someone's shadow.
That silhouette wasn't a student's.
From the necktie flapping in the wind, he knew right away it was a teacher.
The teacher was far off, but seemed to be watching Kawahara closely.
You see, someone had told on him for acting strange.
So the teacher had followed him up there.
The teacher came closer, one step at a time.
That mouth clearly looked like it wanted to say something.
And the teacher's eyes were fixed on the textbook in Kawahara's hands.
With every step closer, the shadow grew bigger.
Kawahara felt like the shadow was going to swallow him, and before he knew it, he shoved the teacher away and ran.{p}

"Hold it☆"
After something like that, a teacher couldn't just let it slide, right?
Kawahara got chased.
And while he was running, he tripped near the stairs.
The textbook fell out of his hands.
It tumbled all the way down to the bottom of the stairs.
Whatever was inside must have fallen out down there.
If what was in the textbook was a question sheet, they'd never believe him, no matter what he said.
Kawahara stood at the top of the stairs, feeling hopeless.{p}

He swayed, and his body lost its balance.
He fell headfirst down the stairs.{p}

...Naturally, his neck broke.
He died.
...They say next to Kawahara's body were the textbook and a letter that had been tucked inside it.
What was in his textbook wasn't a question sheet at all.
When the teacher picked it up and looked, it was a love letter.
It seems the guy who borrowed Kawahara's textbook didn't go return it himself.{p}

I bet it was Hashimoto, who wrote this apology letter saying, 'It's my fault Kawahara died'... I bet she offered to return it for him, and tucked the love letter inside.
The reason Koizumi was messing with Kawahara's textbook was to look at that love letter.
I don't know why he did it.
Maybe he saw Hashimoto slip the letter in and got curious, or maybe there was some other reason.
I think Kawahara's death was his own fault.
That's what he gets for thinking all those needless things.{p}

Still, it was awful for Hashimoto too, the one who wrote the love letter.
She probably never imagined her letter would lead to something like this.
Everyone around her made a big fuss, and I hear she had a really hard time.
Kawahara had other fans too, see, so she got harassed and stuff.
The rumor is that Hashimoto killed herself after writing this apology letter.
And so, the textbook and the love letter in question were given a proper memorial service and burned.
But I guess some kind of lingering obsession latched onto them.
Apparently, even now, a phantom of that textbook sometimes appears in this school.{p}
Anyone who sees it is sure to meet with misfortune..........Ah!{p}
{b}, behind you...☆

...Huh?
There was nothing unusual there.
And yet she ran off as if terrified.
"Fukuza...!"
She opened the door and dashed out.
"Wait!"
As I went to chase after her, someone grabbed my hand.{p}

When I looked, a stranger was standing beside me.
Who is this boy?
When did he get in here★
He pulled hard on my arm.
What was happening to me?
My mind went completely blank.{p}

Next, darkness spread out before my eyes.
Here and there in the darkness, I could see glimmers of light.{p}

Now and then, a shaft of light lit up his face.
Could this be... the Kawahara that Fukuzawa was talking about...?
There was no one else around anymore.
Such deep darkness...
It felt like it would swallow me and I'd melt away.
He turned toward me, looking like he wanted to say something.
His lips, redder than anyone else's, trembled slightly.
And I silently waited for his words...{p}

No good?
But doesn't everybody want to go home?
This is the first time I've ever stayed at school this late.
Let's go home, okay? It's decided.
I'll tell you my story some other time.
I'm Reiko Fukuzawa.
I'm in Class 1-G, okay?{p}

Hmm.
So you're actually pretty gutsy, {b}.
Well, you are putting together a scary-story feature for the newspaper club.
I guess you'd have to be, huh.
But still, even without scary stories, going to school is such a drag, right?{p}

"Fukuzawa, you look for one."
I said it more or less on a whim.
"Mmm, okay, but you look too, {b}."
At that, I reluctantly glanced around.
I opened some random file and looked inside.{p}

Let's see...
"I did not do any bullying like the teacher says.
But I got yelled at, so I am writing this.
It's true I hit the kid in the seat next to me, but only a little.
I am very sorry.
The end."
I don't know who wrote it, but what a ridiculous letter.{p}

I'm kind of tired.
Maybe I'll take a little nap.
..............................Ah!
This is no time to be saying that.
I have to do this interview properly.
The seventh person hasn't even shown up, and if I miss this story too, we'll be down to five wonders.
I don't want Hino yelling at me.
Um, let me try reading one of these files lying around.{p}
I'll look for a different file.{p}

"What's wrong, {b}?
You're making a funny face."
Fukuzawa came over.
"Was there something written in that file?
...Oh."
She looked at the file in my hand and fell silent for a while.{p}

I see.
So you've never had that kind of experience, {b}.
I haven't really either.
I mean, if I don't like something, I just say so, flat out.
But Kawahara was the kind of person who couldn't do that.
He'd be all smiles with his teachers and friends, while sticking his tongue out at them on the inside.{p}

Can't guess?
It was a chemistry textbook.
Remember, I said Kawahara had lent his textbook to someone?
That one.{p}
Nope.{p}

At the next break, he went to the teacher.
"It's about the missing question sheet."
When he said that, the teacher showed him into this reflection room.
When he opened the textbook in the reflection room, sure enough, there was a question sheet inside.
The one Koizumi had secretly slipped in.
Kawahara told the whole story, start to finish.
But the teacher didn't believe a word he said.
The teacher said there'd be no scolding, and told him to just write an apology letter right here.
What a joke, right?
If he did that, he'd be admitting he was the culprit.
Maybe the teacher meant to get that as proof and then do something to him.
That thought popped into his head.{p}

He ran.
Why wouldn't anyone believe him?
Could it be they knew how he was always cursing everyone in his head?
That's what he was thinking as he went.
He just got more and more frantic.

"Whoa!"
In the hallway, he crashed into Koizumi.
"You☆"
Kawahara went for Koizumi with his fists.
He screamed at him, demanding to know why he was trying to frame him.
They say Koizumi just laughed.
"What're you freaking out about? Just tell 'em it wasn't you, right?
Or what, they didn't believe you?
Kawahara, that's your own fault, isn't it?
All you ever do is put on a nice front.
That's why nobody believes you when it counts!"
Kawahara just snapped.
He shoved Koizumi to the floor and punched him over and over.
Right then, the teacher caught up.
"Kawahara! What are you doing?"{p}
He ran away again.

A girl in the hallway was screaming.
Well, of course she was.
Kawahara, the model student, had suddenly started beating someone up.
"Kawahara! Get back here☆"
The teacher was shouting.
Kawahara ran all the way home that day.{p}

...The next day.
He was absent from school.
But when his homeroom teacher called his house, they were told he'd left for school.
He must have run away from home.
The teachers looked for him.
They went to the police, and searched the school buildings too.
If he'd run away and was hiding, it might be the lodge at school, or the tatami room in the old school building...
They searched every place they could think of, but he was nowhere to be found.
In the end, they filed a missing person report with the police.
His parents were worried sick.
But he stayed missing.
Then, about a week later...
A student had to use the reflection room for some petty rule violation.
When they went into the reflection room, someone was sitting there, facing the window, perfectly still.
"Hey, you. Mind stepping out for a bit?"
When the teacher reached out, the student by the window toppled over.{p}

...It was Kawahara.
They say his left wrist was covered in cuts.
He'd hidden in the reflection room and slit his wrist over and over, apparently.
I heard that if you want to kill yourself by cutting your wrists, you have to cut really deep.
Apparently not much blood comes out.
But the cuts on Kawahara's wrist were really, really deep.
They say he filled some bowl he got from somewhere with water and kept his wrist soaking in it.
When he was found, he'd apparently been dead for several days.{p}

And the last thing he wrote... should be in that file there.
{b}, let me see that a sec.
See, it's filed down near the bottom.
"...Why won't anyone believe what I say?
I can't trust the teacher.
And I can't trust myself either, for agonizing over something like this."
They say Kawahara killed himself after writing this.{p}

Actually, after Kawahara, one more student died here.
Hashimoto, the one who wrote the apology letter saying it was her fault he died.
You see, the reason Koizumi slipped the question sheet into Kawahara's textbook was Hashimoto.
Koizumi liked Hashimoto, apparently.
And Hashimoto, well, she liked Kawahara.
You get it, right?
Koizumi got jealous and played a nasty trick on Kawahara...
They say Hashimoto died in almost exactly the same way Kawahara did.
And because that became such a big issue, the reflection room stopped being used.
They say the key was put away inside Kawahara's coffin, but...
So why was a key like that lying in the hallway?
You don't think a ghost or something lured us here...
Just kidding. I'm overthinking it, right?
I don't have anything to apologize for, anyway.
And I've never let things eat at me like that, either.{p}

Okay, let's head back to the club room soon.
This room is kind of creepy, don't you think?
I don't want to stay in here too long.
If the seventh person hasn't come to the club room, let's just go home.{p}

Oh, but {b}, you said the people around you decide what you're like on their own, right?
Maybe you've got something in common with Kawahara?
Huh, not as bad as him?
You should still be careful, though.
I think that means you've got a weak spot.
And maybe it's not just people... ghosts might find it easy to get their hooks into you too.{p}

Ahahaha...
Sorry, sorry, did I say something mean?
Hey, let's get back to the club room already.
The seventh one might be there by now.{p}Let's hurry.
I'll lock this place up again, okay?{p}
